notes: FOU-99 v1 iOS — chip-based classifier sourced from the authoritative pocketpal-website APPLE_DEVICES table; tier candidates extrapolated from the Android bench campaign (no iOS benches yet). iOS classifier: utsname.machine → chip → soc_class → tier. Apple chip lineage is linear, so this collapses ~85 device identifiers onto ~20 chip names. RAM bands are tighter than Android because iOS reports physicalMemory close to nominal (no ~30% Android-style undercount).
_status_note: Classifier (device_id_to_chip, chip_to_class, tier_matrix) is firm — sourced from pocketpal-website/lib/device-lookup.ts. obs_tg_estimate values are EXTRAPOLATED from Android bench data on architecturally-equivalent SoCs (e.g. A18 Pro / A19 Pro ≈ SD 8 Gen 5 → flagship anchor; A15/A16/M1 ≈ SD 8 Gen 2 → high anchor; A14 ≈ Tensor G4 → mid anchor). An iOS bench campaign is pending and will replace these with measured values.
_quant_policy: On iOS, Metal is the only accelerated backend (no Hexagon HTP). Metal does not give Q4_0 a meaningful PP fastpath over Q4_K_M, so Q4_K_M is primary across all tiers. Q4_0 may still be listed as an alternate where the file is published, mainly for users wanting smaller download / lower peak memory on tight devices.

classifier._comment_layer_1: Layer 1: utsname.machine device id → chip name. App reads sysctlbyname('hw.machine') on iOS (returns e.g. 'iPhone16,1') and looks up the chip. Sourced from the curated APPLE_DEVICES table in pocketpal-website/lib/device-lookup.ts (the same identifier-to-marketing-name map used by the benchmarks site). Covers iPhone 8 onward (A11+) and all iPads from iPad mini 5 / Air 3 onward.
classifier._comment_layer_2: Layer 2: chip name → soc_class. Apple chip generations cluster cleanly. A10-A13 are entry by today's LLM-on-mobile standards (≤4 GiB RAM, sub-A15 NE). A14/A15/A16/A18-base are mid (mainline non-Pro of their era, but no Pro-tier cores). A17 Pro / A18 Pro / A19 / A19 Pro / M-series are flagship.
classifier._comment_layer_3: Layer 3: unknown-chip fallback. When utsname.machine isn't in device_id_to_chip (new device released after this rules version), fall back to numeric heuristics on the model identifier. iPhone NN,M with NN ≥ 18 → flagship (we're well into A19+ era); iPad NN,M with NN ≥ 16 + RAM ≥ 8 GiB → flagship. Older unknowns fall back to 'mid' as a safe middle ground.

rules.rationale: iPhone17+ in id terms = iPhone 16/17 line and later; assume A18 Pro-class or newer.
iPhone15-17 id range covers A16/A17/A18 non-Pro; mid by default.
Recent iPad with ≥8 GiB → M-series or A17 Pro class.

classifier._comment_matrix: Tier matrix: (ram_band × soc_class) → tier_id. Same 4 output tiers as Android. RAM bands are tighter than Android because iOS reports physicalMemory close to nominal.

low.description: Entry tier — sub-1B models only. iOS anchors (estimated): A12/A13 iPhones with 3-4 GiB RAM (iPhone XR/XS/11/SE 2). Q4_K_M primary throughout; Metal has no Q4_0 fastpath that would justify swapping. iOS apps are killed aggressively above ~1.5 GB resident, so we stay strictly below that.

mid.description: Mid tier — adds Bonsai-1.7B. iOS anchors (estimated): A14/A15 iPhones with 4-6 GiB RAM (iPhone 12/13/14 non-Pro). Cross-platform GGUF works; Bonsai-Q1_0 is supported by upstream llama.cpp b9204+ (PocketPal iOS llama.rn version must match).

high.description: High tier — adds SmolLM3-3B. iOS anchors (estimated): A16/A18 iPhones with 6-8 GiB RAM (iPhone 14 Pro / 15 / 16). Q4_K_M is primary (Metal Q4_K_M ≈ Q4_0); the listing intentionally omits Q4_0 to keep the shortlist focused.

flagship.description: Flagship tier — adds 3-4B mid/q4 models. iOS anchors (estimated): A17 Pro / A18 Pro / A19 / M-series with 8+ GiB RAM (iPhone 15 Pro+, iPad Pro M-series). Memory headroom is ample (M-series iPads have 8-32 GiB) but iOS jetsam is still a factor — peak load of 4-5 GB is realistic.

_extrapolation_notes.method: iOS TG estimates are taken from Android bench medians on architecturally-comparable Snapdragons. Mappings used: A18 Pro / A19 → SD 8 Elite Gen 5 / SM8850 (Myron); A17 Pro / A18 / M2 → SD 8 Gen 3 (no exact Android peer, interpolated between Myron and S23); A15 / A16 / M1 → SD 8 Gen 2 / SM8550 (S23); A14 → Tensor G4 (mid); A13 → Helio G88 (low).
known_limitations: Metal backend behavior on Q4_K_M vs Q4_0 has not been measured here. If iOS bench finds Metal Q4_0 wins by >10% on TG, candidates will be re-ordered. Mitigation: app code should treat order as preference, not contract.
iOS jetsam (per-app memory ceiling) may kill larger models that the rules say fit. Peak load estimates from Android may understate iOS pressure. Conservative min_ram_gb values applied.
Bonsai Q1_0 kernel performance on Metal is unknown — Q1_0 is a slow-path kernel even on x86/ARM CPU; Metal port may or may not exist for Q1_0 yet.
Mac (macOS) targets are out of scope for this file. If PocketPal ships on Mac, M-series performance ≈ flagship iPad.
v2_followups: Run iOS bench campaign on at least one device per soc_class (A13/A14 = entry, A15/A16 = mid, A17 Pro / A18 Pro / M-series = flagship). Replace obs_tg_estimate with measured obs_tg_anchor.
Decide on Metal Q4_0 vs Q4_K_M primary based on actual measurements.
Add a separate iPadOS overlay if iPad-on-iOS-rules diverge (e.g. M-series iPads with 32 GiB unlocking 8B+ candidates that no iPhone could run).
